description: Welcome to STS-51L! Honoring the educational legacy of Space Shuttle Challenger, we are building an interactive space mission simulator that lets students experience real aerospace engineering from concept to operation. Players design spacecraft, choose launch vehicles, and manage strict budgets, mass, power, and orbital limits—seeing firsthand how every trade-off shapes mission success or failure. Join us if you love coding, game design, or space science!
summary:
STS-51L: Deep Space Mission Director is an interactive, browser-based aerospace engineering simulator designed to bridge the gap between oversimplified STEM activities and complex orbital mechanics. Named in honor of Space Shuttle Challenger's educational legacy, the game places students directly in the seat of a NASA Flight Director-challenging them to design, launch, and manage a complete space mission from initial blueprint to deep-space operation.

Before ignition, players choose between four real destinations-Low Earth Orbit, the Lunar South Pole, Mars, and Jupiter's moon Europa-each governed by unique budget caps, radiation belts, and solar irradiance drop-offs. To succeed, students must balance competing engineering constraints across launch vehicle lift limits, payload mass, solar arrays versus plutonium nuclear RTGs, radiation shielding, and Deep Space Network communications.

Once launched, players guide their spacecraft through an animated, five- stage live flight campaign, making split-second resource decisions during in-flight emergencies like solar storms and trajectory drift. This hands-on approach is important because it transforms abstract physics equations into tangible, high-stakes decisions-showing young learners firsthand how real aerospace trade-offs determine whether a mission succeeds or aborts back to Earth.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
STS-51L: Deep Space Mission Director is an interactive, browser-based space mission simulator that lets students act as NASA Flight Directors—designing, launching, and managing a complete mission from concept to operation. Players choose from four real destinations (Low Earth Orbit, the Lunar South Pole, Mars, and Jupiter’s moon Europa) and assemble a spacecraft across five competing subsystems: Launch Vehicles, Power Systems, Radiation Shielding, Communications Arrays, and Scientific Instruments.

Once launched, players watch their spacecraft travel across an animated HTML5 Canvas trajectory from Earth to their target planet through five distinct mission phases (Max-Q Liftoff, Deep Space Navigation, Solar Storm Transit, Orbital Capture, and Final Science Transmission). At each stage, players face interactive emergencies where split-second resource choices determine whether the mission continues or aborts back to Earth.

Creativity, Factors Considered & Intended Impact
Most space STEM content either oversimplifies mission design or buries learners in complex orbital equations. Our simulator makes genuine engineering trade-offs tangible and fun—such as accounting for inverse-square solar power drop-offs at Mars (70%) and Europa (25%) versus the high cost and mass of a Plutonium Nuclear RTG, as well as Deep Space Network antenna range limits and Jovian radiation belts. By providing instant visual telemetry, branching crisis consequences, and a ranked engineering grade (S through F), the game inspires students to experiment, learn from failure, and understand how real aerospace trade-offs shape mission success.

Tools, Languages & Disclosures
Built as a zero-install web application using HTML5 Canvas, CSS3, and JavaScript, hosted live on GitHub Pages. Used AI a little bit for error-checking, help, and overall structure.
